main_text.p: Sal Ammoniacus est Sal fossilis, amarissimus, sub arena ardentissima in Cyrenaica erutus: unde etiam Cyrenaicus dicitur.Sal Ammoniacus.
Sal Gemma est Sal fossilis, e fodinis erutus, Cristalli in morem translucens & candidus.Sal Gemma.

Sal Nitrum seu Petrosum est, quod ex coagulato humore in locis subterraneis humidis instar stiriae salsae dependet, aut instar frigoris congelati in parietibus nitet. Hodie etiam arte Nitrum colligitur.Sal Nitrum.
Sal Indicus est Sal quadantenus nigricans, vel subrufus, in India ex monte Oremeno excisus.Sal Indicus.

Extra terram Sal repertus effoditur ex aquis, & dicitur vel Fontalis, quando fontis rivuli calore Solis siccati, in salem convertuntur: vel Fluvialis, quando fluvius aliquis ramenta fert, quae in salem densantur: vel Stagnalis a Stagnis, quae sale aestuant. vel denique Marinus, quando in extremis littoribus tenuis quidam Sal gignitur.
Sal coctus fit ex aquis, vel marinis, fluvialibus, lacustribus, salsis fontanis, putealibus, vel etiam ex muria nativaSal coctus.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are catchwords-style headings repeating the terms in the text (Sal Ammoniacus, Sal Gemma, Sal Nitrum, Sal Indicus, Sal coctus); they are transcribed as notes at their places. The bottom word "tiva" completes "nativa" across the line; the final line is cut by the page edge and is a fragment, so its word "nativa" is given whole. Faint show-through text is ignored. Hyphenation and some letters (long s, ligatures) are rendered as plain letters; the scan is faded in places, so exact spacing of the margin notes is approximate.
